hints: Differentiate displacement $s(t)$ once to find velocity $v(t)$, and a second time to find acceleration $a(t)$.
Set $a(t) = 0$ to find the time $t$ when acceleration vanishes.
Substitute this time into the velocity expression $v(t)$.
walkthrough:
Differentiate the displacement function $s = t^3 - 6t^2 + 4t$ with respect to $t$ to obtain velocity:
$$v = \frac{ds}{dt} = 3t^2 - 12t + 4$$

Differentiate velocity with respect to $t$ to obtain acceleration:
$$a = \frac{dv}{dt} = 6t - 12$$

Set the acceleration to zero to find the instant of interest:
$$6t - 12 = 0 \implies 6t = 12 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
State the definition of velocity as the derivative of displacement with respect to time:
$$v(t) = \frac{ds}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(t^3 - 6t^2 + 4t\right) = 3t^2 - 12t + 4$$

State the definition of acceleration as the derivative of velocity with respect to time:
$$a(t) = \frac{dv}{dt} = \frac{d}{dt}\left(3t^2 - 12t + 4\right) = 6t - 12$$

Find the time when acceleration is zero:
$$a(t) = 0 \implies 6t - 12 = 0$$
Add $12$ to both sides and divide by $6$:
$$6t = 12 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$$

Substitute $t = 2\text{ s}$ into the velocity equation:
$$v(2) = 3 \times 2^2 - 12 \times 2 + 4$$
$$3 \times 4 = 12$$
$$12 \times 2 = 24$$
$$v(2) = 12 - 24 + 4 = -8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

ai_rubric.Differentiating Motion Functions: Differentiates twice to get $v = 3t^2 - 12t + 4$ and $a = 6t - 12$, solves $a = 0 \implies t = 2\text{ s}$, and finds $v = -8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
